newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African financial index hits new records.
newsitem.headline: South African financial index hits new records.

text.p: South Africa's financial index raced to new record highs on Wednesday, buoyed by positive sentiment and good earnings prospects, but analysts said the sector was nearing its peak.

The all-financial index hit 8,800.6, beating its previous life trading high of 8,793.3 set on April 8. For the past two days it has set new closing highs of 8,727 points on Tuesday and 8,695 on Monday. At 1130 GMT it looked set for another closing record as it was trading at 8,800.5.

But analysts said the sector was nearing its peak as it braces itself for an imminent banking results season over which profit-taking may enter the market and as industrial shares are expected to start luring interest away.
"There is a general bullishness about the sector, but it has got to be tempered because it is near the peak," said David Southey, analyst at Edey Rogers.
Analysts said there was a host of reasons for the sector's rapid advances in 1997.
Last year the whole Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) was hampered by dismal share price performances stemming from the rand's depreciation that began last February.

The financial index was particularly depressed due to two interest rate hikes and worries about the liquidity squeeze in the money market. However, analysts said the sector had defied predictions and still posted healthy results.

"While the market was expecting disastrous results the banks still performed well... there was an overreaction last year and we are seeing a readjustment this year," said Justin Kretzschmar, analyst at SocGen Frankel Pollack.
"It has moved in anticipation of good results to come and off the back of a poor performance last year," he added.

Analysts said there had been a good mix of local institutional and foreign buying in the sector. Overseas investors were especially eyeing major blue chips such as First National Bank Ltd, Amalgamated banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) and Nedcor Ltd.
Some one-off factors have also helped boost the index.

There has been a wealth of speculation surrounding FNB on fresh rumours that a hefty stake in the firm is to be sold off, possibly to a foreign investor such as Barclays Plc and Hong Kong Shanghai Bank.

The firm's share has risen from a trading low of 19.90 rand in December to about 32.00 rand now, despite FNB saying there is no substance in talk that Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd is set to sell off its 20.4 percent holding.
But the share rise has helped the whole index up. "FNB has been largely been driven by rumours in the market for an international tie-up," Kretzschmar said.

Another single-story boost behind the index is a complex deal between Board of Executors Ltd BOEJ.J, NBS Holdings Ltd and Boland Bank Holdings Ltd which will create South Africa's fifth largest banking group.

NBS has risen from 57.00 rand in January to more than 80.00 rand now, BOE has jumped from 80.00 rand at the start of the year to 127.00 rand and Boland has soared to about 52.00 rand from 38.50 rand at the start of February.
Kretzschmar said the firms were benefiting from good sentiment on the deal, but had to deliver the goods. "Now the companies have to justify the price with performance," he said.
